thread:
jordan: Quick design huddle about key rotation UX. Problem: customers running scheduled rotations get confused when "last rotated" shows the job user instead of the service owner. Thoughts?

tess: We should surface both: "Last rotated by <actor> on <timestamp> (rotated via scheduled job)". Screen readers need a concise label, maybe aria-label: 'Rotation history, last rotated by automation on date X'.

maya: Also consider a small badge when rotation is automated: 'Auto-rotate' with tooltip linking to rotation policy. That helps differentiate human vs automated actions.

lucas: UX corner case: if rotation fails (job error), show amber state 'Rotation failed' with link to logs and a 'Retry' button. Don't automatically retry without user consent.

jordan: Good. Copy for failed state: 'Automated rotation failed — view logs or retry manually.' Keep CTA order: logs first, retry secondary to encourage investigation.

devbot: Note: rotation jobs post events to audit log: rotation:status:job_id:result. Make sure UI surfaces job_id on detail for support.

tess: Accessibility: for the 'Auto-rotate' badge include an accessible name: 'Auto-rotate enabled. Click for details.' and keyboard focusable.

maya: I'll add small UI in key detail: rotation badge, last rotated by + timestamp (with parenthetical 'via scheduler' when applicable), and a compact rotation history list collapsed by default.

jordan: Could we add a quick 'snooze auto-rotate' action for maintainers? Might be handy during incident.

lucas: That needs policy guardrails but a short-lived snooze (e.g., 1h) could work. Add a confirm modal.

jordan: OK will prototype with snooze option and rotation health indicator. Thanks team.
